title: Decisions
subtitle: Questions the agent is not allowed to settle, and how the owner settled
  them
toc: true
---

The brief lists the decisions that belong to a human: physics modelling choices, licence and
data questions, which properties to prove, use of the compute cluster, and benchmark failures
that aren't explained by a bug. When the agent reaches one, it writes the question down with
context and a recommended answer, carries on with whatever isn't blocked, and waits. Numbers
(OQ-*n*) match the project's internal record. Newest first within each group.

## Awaiting a decision

- **[OQ-17](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-17)**: what licence text the package metadata should carry while no release licence is
  chosen. It blocks nothing while the code is private.

## Settled

### OQ-16 · Kinetic ranges, ITER shapes and the α~MHD~ cap for the M2 datasets {#oq-16}

*Decided 2 Oct 2026.* The owner set one dataset per machine, MAST-U and ITER. The geometry
ranges were measured ([OQ-15](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-15)); the kinetic ranges, the ion species and a cap on the normalised
pressure gradient α~MHD~ were proposed by the agent from memory and needed a decision before
any data was generated. Three questions: (a) do the kinetic ranges and ions stand per machine;
(b) is one ITER plasma shape with the current ramp-up's q profiles enough, or should 15 MA
baseline equilibria be added first; (c) a fixed cap, a cap that depends on the magnetic shear,
or sampling α~MHD~ in place of β~e~.

**Decision.** (a) Approved as proposed for both machines: D and carbon for MAST-U, D-T as one
ion of mean mass and neon for ITER (ranges in [datasets](technical/datasets.qmd#sampling-space)).
(b) One shape is enough for version 1; the missing baseline is recorded as a limit ([K-016](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-016)) and
baseline shapes come before an ITER version 2. (c) Fixed caps for version 1 (MAST-U 4, ITER 2),
a shear-dependent cap to follow ([K-017](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-017)). The two datasets were generated the same day
([entry 17](log/17-tglf-datasets-mastu-iter.qmd)).

### OQ-15 · Sampling ranges and TGLF settings for MAST-U {#oq-15}

*Decided 2 Oct 2026.* MAST-U is outside both surrogates TORAX ships with (aspect ratio fixed at
3, or elongation up to 1.5). The agent proposed ranges from memory, not checked against a
source. **Decision:** the agent measures the geometry ranges on equilibria rather than choosing
them, and the kinetic ranges go to a physics check (became [OQ-16](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-16)); a second region besides
MAST-U, each tagged so it can be selected alone or pooled (became the ITER dataset); TGLF with
the SAT2 saturation rule and both magnetic perturbations; CGYRO spot checks of TGLF at M4.
Measured, the MAST-U geometry is narrower in shape than the proposal (triangularity on
interior surfaces at most 0.24, not 0.6).

### OQ-14 · One cluster job to check TGLF and time it {#oq-14}

*Decided 2 Oct 2026.* TGLF's licence was settled by the owner's pointer to the public GACODE
repository (Apache-2.0). The remaining install check, TGLF as TORAX's transport model, could not
run on a login node. **Approved:** one CPU node for at most 30 minutes, running TORAX's TGLF
tests, a TORAX step with TGLF, CGYRO's regression suite, and TGLF on a few hundred points of
the sampling space to measure the cost per case. *Outcome*
([entry 16](log/16-tglf-build-and-cost.qmd)): [TGLF 9/9 regression cases; tglf2py wrapper 11/11; TORAX TGLF transport-model tests 3/3; CGYRO 21/21]{.claim}[C-069](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-069){.cid .st-measured}; [2.2-2.5 s per case alone, 2.6 s median in a 64-worker pool; about 700 core-hours per 10^6 cases]{.claim}[C-068](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-068){.cid .st-measured}; the
TORAX step with TGLF failed ([fails at the first step: NaN fluxes on the axis face, about 10^6 gyro-Bohm units on the edge face ([K-015](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-015))]{.claim}[C-070](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-070){.cid .st-measured}, [K-015](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-015)). The first submission failed at
start-up on a shell setting in the job script, with no compute used, and was resubmitted.

### M1 physicist review {#m1-review}

*Passed 1 Oct 2026.* The last M1 acceptance criterion is a review by a physicist. The owner did
the review as reviewer of record. The agent set out six items, each with its evidence and a
recommendation; **the owner accepted all six recommendations as written.**

1. **Benchmark tolerance**, against RAPTOR on the published ITER L-mode case ([OQ-12](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-12)): the
   t = 10 s profiles within 2% for T~i~, T~e~, ψ and q, and within 0.1% for the densities; the
   line-averaged temperature and density traces within 5% over 0–10 s. The fusion and Ohmic
   powers are reported, not gated: the paper's two codes differ by 13–22% on the alpha
   ion/electron split. Result at the published settings: [T_i 1.23% (1.1%), T_e 0.28% (0.71%), n_e 0.03% (0.03%), psi 0.49% (0.41%), q 0.69% (0.70%)]{.claim}[C-050](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-050){.cid .st-reviewed}; transient
   [2.4% at dt = 0.05 s, 2.9% at dt = 0.00625 s (1.0% at t = 10 s)]{.claim}[C-053](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-053){.cid .st-reviewed}. Both pass.
2. **TORAX version.** The differences between the paper's TORAX run and TORAX 1.4.3
   ([T_i 0.13%, T_e 0.50%, n_e 0.01%, psi 0.08%, q 0.16%; Ohmic power density 3.6%]{.claim}[C-051](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-051){.cid .st-reviewed}) are accepted as a code-version effect.
3. **Pedestal.** The fixed-pedestal model's pinning source removes [87–98%]{.claim}[C-038](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-038){.cid .st-reviewed} of the
   heating in the ITER hybrid ramp-up. Accepted for core profiles inside ρ = 0.9; power
   crossing the edge is not taken from these runs ([K-010](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-010)). Revisited at M3.
4. **Time step.** The ITER hybrid example settings are not converged in time ([entry
   3](log/03-fixed-step-loop.qmd)). They are used only to check the wrapper. Runs used as a
   physics reference use a step at which halving it changes the core temperature by at most 1%
   after the first 5 s. Solver stalls stay reported ([OQ-5](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)).
5. **ASCOT5 alpha source.** Orbit tolerance 10^-7^ ([0.348 at 10^-6^, 0.331 at 10^-7^]{.claim}[C-058](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-058){.cid .st-reviewed} of the birth power to
   ions at 10^-6^ and 10^-7^); 640 markers give the total ([72.2 MW vs 70.5 MW]{.claim}[C-059](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-059){.cid .st-reviewed} against TORAX's
   local model) and the electron/ion split, and the radial shape waits for the production run
   ([OQ-13](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-13)). Holding the source fixed for 2 s is accepted ([+0.03% in stored energy (central T_e +0.5%, T_e and T_i profiles 0.6%)]{.claim}[C-060](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-060){.cid .st-reviewed}). The small excess
   in the markers' birth power ([K-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-011)) is to be explained before neutral-beam ions are added.
6. **Fallback, pedestal and sawtooth models**: [OQ-1](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-1) below.

The claims these items judged are marked *reviewed* in the [claims register](claims.qmd).

### OQ-1 · The fallback transport model {#oq-1}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026, at the M1 physicist review.* M0 needed a toy transport model to exercise
the loop, and a smooth critical-gradient form was used. **The trusted fallback for real runs is
TORAX's Bohm/gyro-Bohm model**, which is already the fallback behind the guard inside TORAX. The
critical-gradient form stays as the closure of the Tokamak Toolkit's own analytic test loop only. For M1 the
pedestal is TORAX's fixed pedestal, and sawtooth mixing is represented by a constant
diffusivity near the axis (the ITER examples have no sawtooth model); a sawtooth model is added
when a case needs one.

### OQ-13 · A third ASCOT5 job, for the production run {#oq-13}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* The second ASCOT5 job ([entry 12](log/12-ascot5-second-run.qmd)) finished
its tolerance check but not its production run: a per-marker time limit, set too short by the
agent, stopped [2823 of 6400 markers, 18% of the birth power]{.claim}[C-057](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-057){.cid .st-measured}. **A third job is approved**: up to eight hours on one node,
the production run at the tighter tolerance with no time limit, and a check at a tighter one
still. The M1 physicist review is not held for it.

*Outcome, 2 Oct 2026* ([entry 15](log/15-ascot5-production-run.qmd)). The job ran in 3 h 37 min
and every alpha finished. Total heating: [71.8 MW vs 70.5 MW]{.claim}[C-064](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-064){.cid .st-measured}. The tighter check changed the
heating by [electrons -0.16%, ions +0.08%]{.claim}[C-066](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-066){.cid .st-measured}, so the working tolerance stands. No further job is requested.

### OQ-12 · Which published profiles the benchmark is compared with {#oq-12}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* M1 asks for a match to *published profiles*. The ITER hybrid scenarios
have no published profiles from a second code. The TORAX paper publishes one quantitative
comparison with an independent code, RAPTOR, on an ITER L-mode case, with its full
configuration and the profiles as vector figures. **That case is the M1 physics benchmark**,
compared with both RAPTOR's and the paper's own TORAX curves, first at the published time step
and then at a converged one ([entry 11](log/11-raptor-lmode-benchmark.qmd)). The ITER hybrid
runs remain the stiff-transport and pedestal case. The tolerance was set at the
[M1 physicist review](#m1-review).

### OQ-11 · A second ASCOT5 cluster job {#oq-11}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* The first ASCOT5 job ([entry 10](log/10-ascot5-alpha-heating.qmd))
showed that the orbit tolerance chosen for speed loses alphas that should be confined ([C-043](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-043)),
and that at the tighter tolerance 640 markers resolve the total alpha heating but not its
radial shape ([C-045](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-045)). **A second job is approved**: one node for up to four hours, ten times
more markers at the tighter tolerance, and a check at a tighter one still. Further jobs need
their own approval. Outcome: [entry 12](log/12-ascot5-second-run.qmd) and [OQ-13](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-13).

### OQ-10 · Which radial variable the guard's features use {#oq-10}

*Deferred 1 Oct 2026, to M3.* The guard checks whether a plasma state is inside the region the
surrogate was trained on, using features such as normalised temperature gradients. The Tokamak Toolkit
computes those gradients with respect to the normalised flux radius, scaled by the geometric
minor radius; QLKNN, as TORAX feeds it, uses the midplane minor radius of each surface. On the
ITER hybrid scenario the two differ from [+19%]{.claim}[C-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-032){.cid .st-measured} in the core to about a third at the
edge ([K-008](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-008)). No run is affected yet. **The convention will be chosen when the first trained
surrogate exists (M3)**, and in any case before a verified domain is certified (M4).

### OQ-9 · Fast-ion sources from ASCOT5 {#oq-9}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* **Fusion alphas first**, born from the plasma profiles TORAX computes, as
a direct check against TORAX's own alpha heating. Neutral-beam ions follow once a physicist has
approved the injector geometry. **One short test job on the compute cluster is approved**; each
further job needs its own approval.

### OQ-5 · What "reproduces the benchmark" means {#oq-5}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* Two comparisons: the Tokamak Toolkit's loop against TORAX's own output at the same
settings (a check of the wrapper), and against the published cross-code comparison (a physics
statement). **The wrapper check must agree to 10^-10^** (it passes at round-off: [C-006](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-006), [C-007](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-007)).
**The physics tolerance is set by the physicist reviewer** at the M1 gate (set: see the
[M1 physicist review](#m1-review)). Because the published
reference runs are not converged in time ([entry 3](log/03-fixed-step-loop.qmd), [C-012](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-012), [C-013](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-013)),
**the physics comparison is made at the published settings first**, then at a converged time
step, with the difference reported as its own line in the discrepancy budget. **Solver stalls
stay reported**, not tuned away by relaxing a line-search setting
([entry 5](log/05-stalls-rf-and-builds.qmd), [C-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-011)). **Energy and particles must balance to
10^-6^ per step** on converged steps ([entry 8](log/08-energy-particle-balance.qmd), [C-035](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-035), [C-036](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-036)); the
flat-top reference solver's defect ([C-037](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-037)) is reported, not required to close.

### OQ-3 · Where the code will live {#oq-3}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* **A private hosted repository**, where the continuous-integration
workflow runs on every change. The code stays private; this log is how the work is shown. Until
the workflow has passed, "tested" in the [claims register](claims.qmd) still means "asserted by
a named test, run before each publish".

### OQ-8 · Which machine description for the equilibrium solver {#oq-8}

*Decided 30 Sep 2026.* **MAST-U.** FreeGSNKE's repository already ships a MAST-U-like machine
description (coils, passive structures, limiter, wall; credited to UKAEA) under the same open
licence, so nothing had to be assembled from published drawings. It is fetched from a pinned
upstream version with a checksum per file. This covers the equilibrium work only: the M1
transport benchmark stays with the ITER scenario, because no published TORAX MAST-U scenario
exists and QLKNN was not trained on spherical-tokamak conditions.

### OQ-7 · Input data for a STEP extension {#oq-7}

*Deferred 30 Sep 2026.* Extending the benchmark to a STEP power-plant flat-top is a future
extension, not part of M1. The work stays with the ITER benchmark and MAST-U for now; the data
question reopens if and when the extension is picked up.

### OQ-6 · Which benchmark {#oq-6}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026, amended 30 Sep 2026.* **The ITER hybrid scenario** that ships with
TORAX: an 80-second current ramp-up, and a 5-second flat-top as the quicker check. A planned
STEP extension was deferred on 30 Sep ([OQ-7](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-7)).

### OQ-4 · Newton-Raphson for the coupling loop {#oq-4}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026.* **Approved.** The M0 loop used relaxed Picard iteration, which
oscillates instead of converging once transport becomes stiff: on the toy model's original
settings the residual sat between 3 × 10⁻² and 8 × 10⁻² after 12 iterations. The owner
approved a Newton-Raphson solver with derivatives from automatic differentiation and a fixed
iteration count, keeping Picard as the fallback, and stall reporting for both
([entry 1](log/01-newton-solver.qmd)).

### OQ-2 · Where to run {#oq-2}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026.* Tests and the early milestones run on an interactive node with one
datacentre GPU. Anything longer goes through the cluster's batch system on an allocation the
owner named, and every job is announced to the owner before it is submitted.
